faq.q: How do I hold a pencil?
faq.a: Pinch it between your thumb and pointing finger, and let it rest on your middle finger. Hold it gently, just above the sharpened part.

faq.q: Why does my hand get tired when I write?
faq.a: Often it is from squeezing too hard. Hold the pencil gently, take little breaks and shake your hands out. Tell a grown-up if it keeps hurting.
asks: My hand hurts when I write

faq.q: Is it okay to hold a pencil with four fingers?
faq.a: Yes. Studies found that a four-finger hold can be just as good as three fingers. What matters is that it is comfy and you can write.
A pencil grip is a soft rubber shape that slides onto the pencil and shows your fingers where to go. Some people find it makes writing comfier.

faq.q: How can I make my fingers stronger?
faq.a: Play with play dough, pick up small things with pegs or tweezers, and tear paper into little bits. Fun games build strong fingers.

facts: A common pencil hold pinches the pencil with the thumb and pointing finger, with the pencil resting on the middle finger.
A study of school children found that four-finger pencil holds were as fast and as neat as three-finger holds.
